Liquidating Steinhoff

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
In 2016, Braam Van Huysteen sold his company Tekkietown to Steinhoff for R3.2 billion paid for in Steinhoff shares a year later they were almost worthless. Now the race is on to liquidate Steinhoff

Unique Selling Point:
The main players will speak on camera to Carte Blanche. A David and Goliath story in a race against time

Summary:
Imagine this. You spend a lot of time and money and risk building up your unique company. It starts to do well and gets noticed by Markus Jootse, once South Africa’s darling of the business world. The man who you think, has the Midas touch. Markus makes you and your investors an offer for your company in 2016, and instead of paying you cash he offers you shares in one of the richest companies on the JSE and the Frankfurt stock exchange. You agree, you sign the contracts and you get your shares. You have just sold your company for R3.2 Billion Rand, except you opt for shares in Steinhoff instead of the cash. What could possibly go wrong?

A year later you get to answer that question when Markus Jooste’s global fraud is exposed, and the once mighty Steinhoff empire comes tumbling down. This is what happened to Braam Van Huyssteen when he sold Tekkie Town to Steinhoff for R3.2 Billion rand. Braam did his due diligence, he went through the books. The accountants said the financial statements fairly reflected the value of the company. Except they didn’t. Markus Jooste may as well have given Braam Van Huyssteen fake bank notes for Tekkie Town. But it was too late – Jooste had already taken Tekkie Town’s shares and funneled them into Steinhoff. Van Huysteen and his investors had basically given away the asset to Jooste for nothing.


Further information:
Now three years later, Jooste is still living a life of luxury, reportedly at Lanzerac near Franschoek, and creditors are scrambling around trying to recoup their money.
Complex financial schemes have been put in place in the Netherlands where the bankers look like they will get almost everything back, even though they may have to wait a bit longer than they thought. To make things more opaque Jooste moved Steinhoff International Holdings to the Netherlands.

So where does that leave Braam Van Huysteen? Basically nowhere. For a second time the Tekkie Town guys are being fleeced. They want to try and recover what little they can, but they are in a race against time against Dutch law, Steinhoff and some powerful bankers who want it all. Tekkie Town are looking to recover R1.8 billion rand but they will be squeezed out if the matter is heard in a Dutch court next month.

THE RACE AGAINST TIME AND THE DUTCH
So the Tekkie Town guys are fighting back in a David and Goliath Battle. Last week they launched an urgent application in the Cape High court to have Steinhoff international Holdings liquidated here in South Africa. Former CEO Bernard Mostert signed a comprehensive affidavit that shows just how important this matter still is and the massive effect it can have on many businesses well known to South Africans.

We speak to the main players in what is arguably the biggest case of corporate fraud in South African business history.

Press Release:


Derek Watts: “We're swamped by State Capture exposés showing how billions have been drained from state coffers. But is big business in SA setting a good example? When the Steinhoff scandal exploded in 2017, around R21 billion in public funds were squandered. So far, no arrests have been made in the biggest corporate fraud case in South African history. Now, the battle for payouts begins. Could David beat Goliath and hold the kingpins accountable?”



The Steinhoff Swindle

It’s been three and a half years since the epic crash of retailing giant Steinhoff – the biggest corporate scandal in the country’s history that wiped more than R200 billion off the JSE. The company has admitted unlawful conduct, yet there have been no charges and no prosecutions. Currently, Steinhoff faces about 90 separate legal proceedings in claims that exceed R136 billion. Steinhoff has proposed a global settlement agreement, but some claimants are unhappy with it and are taking their battles to court. In the latest application, the founders of Tekkie Town want to liquidate the retailing giant in the hope of restoring some of what they have lost.

Producer: Joy Summers | Researcher: Tony Beamish | Presenter: Derek Watts

Watch the trailer

Script:


Final script:
Liquidating Steinhoff for TX Sunday 6th June 2021 FACT CHECKED

Commentary One
For a multi-millionaire Braam van Huysteen is a back to basics sort of guy. And that was the philosophy he applied to his business Tekkie Town which he started with one store and R20 000

Braam
We started with one shop in Mossel bay and ended up with 400 stores.
I don’t think we were that very clever, we just worked very hard, we focused on the basics.

Commentary Two
He also created a R100 million rand staff trust for emergencies for his staff. In time it would become a life saver. Landezwa Dulaze was the HR manager

Landezwa Dulaze
Tekkie Town was a fast growing business, a cash generating business, debt free. I mean who doesn’t want to be a part of that business?

Braam up sound
Ek is a tien en a half, en ek is TekkieTown!

Commentary Three
While Van Huyssteen was building his shoe business, Markus Jooste was expanding his Stellenbosch based furniture retailer Steinhoff, into a global empire. Steinhoff had already bought Pepkor from Christo Wiese, for 5.7 billion dollars, making Wiese the biggest Steinhoff shareholder and it’s chairman. Then Steinhoff made an offer to Braam for Tekkie Town.

DEREK
Now you obviously had done your due diligence, you knew and trusted Markus Jooste?
Braam
My due diligence more consisted out of following Dr Weise – because who am I to argue with what he was doing? Everything looked fine to me.

Commentary Four
Bernard Mostert was Braam’s trusted CEO of Tekkie Town. He was excited by the prospect of taking Tekkie Town global.

Derek
So you had faith in Steinhoff?
We had faith in the system and a lot of faith in Steinhoff, ya




LINK
Then in 2016 they sold Tekkie Town lock stock and takkies to Steinhoff for R3.25 Billion rand. But they didn’t get it in cash, they got it in Steinhoff shares and the deal locked them in for three years.

Commentary five
Around that time a single Steinhoff share was worth a princely sum of R96, 85. But just over a year later, Braam and Bernard woke up to the biggest corporate scandal in SA history, and Steinhoff shares were crashing

Bernard
I thought it was corporate politics. I never imagined that we stood on the precipice of SA’s one of the largest corporate frauds in history

Commentary Six
Marcus Jooste and a small group of executives at Steinhoff had created fictitious profits of R106 billion. Today a Steinhoff share will cost you less than R2-00.

Derek
As it turns out they may as well have paid you in counterfeit notes?
Bernard
Absolutely because the value that we were presented with was based on the company’s own admission of misrepresentation of nearly R106 billion rand. The company calls it unlawful conduct. I agree with that.

Commentary seven
Rob Rose is the editor of the Financial Mail and has written a detailed book on Steinhoff

Derek
Rob just give us a sense of the scale of the fraud and the impact it’s had in SA and globally?
Rob
It’s the kind of event that cascades through the entire corporate sector, it’s made auditors far more wary of signing off statements, but it did cause a real loss and it’s not just the R250 billion in value that vanished off the stock market in a week, its far deeper – its created a deep wound in our corporate sector and it going to be quite hard and take quite a long time to heal.
Derek
Van Huysteen and Mostert infer they sold their business on a lie?
Rob
They certainly were buying into a lie, but it was not just Van Huysteen and Tekkie Town, your pension funds for example Alan Gray and Coronation they also bought into it.

Derek
Now Braam when it happened, did you pick up the phone and speak to Marcus Jooste?
Braam
Before I could pick up the phone he sent me a text message to say he will never look me in the eye again. And within two hours he was at my dining room table and he looked me in the eye a tear ran down his cheek, and he said I am very sorry for involving you in all of this. The first thing that came across me, is that the bible I live by says 70 x 7 times I must forgive

Commentary eight
But forgiveness may have been a little easier for Van Huyssteen, because long before Steinhoff crashed, he had sold 42% of Tekkie Town for $65 million dollars

Braam
I felt like an aircraft went down and I walked away from the accident scene alive.
Derek
You still had some money, you had R1.5 billion or so?
Braam
I had R700 million rand and anyone who sleeps uncomfortable with that kind of money I think is unreasonable. But it wasn’t just me and the R700 million. I had a team, and that is what concerned me most.

Commentary nine
And that is when the staff trust came to the rescue of some of his employees.

Lendezwa
Braam is the main shareholder who established the business, but we all contributed to the business, we felt as staff that we were also defrauded

Commentary ten
But six months after the crash, Van Huyssteen left Steinhoff, and 110 Tekkie Town staff went with him. It was time to start all over again

Lendezwa
As a team we are not the kind that sits around and waits for something to happen

Commentary eleven
In October 2018 Van Huysteen & Mostert and the 110 staff started their new venture, Mr. Tekkie. But Van Huysteen still wanted Tekkie Town back.

Braam
Although we are forgiving in nature, people mustn’t understand our forgiving nature as a weakness. Our business, through fraud, has been taken from us, and we believe it is the right thing to fight tooth and nail to get it restored.

LINK
Fast forward to May 2021 and Braam and Bernard are taking on the David role in the battle with Goliath and have urgently applied to liquidate Steinhoff

Commentary Twelve
There are claims against Steinhoff of R136 billion rand. It’s proposed a global settlement to pay out only about R18 billion rand. But not everyone will be equally compensated. Christo Wiese, the biggest loser in the collapse will get 18.7 cents in the rand. Braam and Bernard and the pension funds however will only get 5 cents in the rand.

Derek
Why is Christo getting a higher payout?
Braam
I wish I knew! I don’t understand that. I say share it up evenly

Commentary Thirteen
Christo Wiese says he is not being unfairly advantaged in fact he told us he’s made a concession.

Christo Wiese up sound
People in a similar position to mine are getting 36 cents in the rand. It’s because I agreed to that amount to bring things to finality. I made a concession.

Commentary fourteen
But their real anger is towards what Bernard calls the vulture investors. He says these international companies swooped in after the crash, bought up the debt, used Tekkie town as collateral, and now Steinhoff will pay them 100 cents in the rand plus interest.

Derek
So it’s the so called vulture investors who win?
Bernard
They win over, and over, and over again, and that money flows out of the country

Commentary Fifteen
If they win their court battle they hope the court will order an insolvency inquiry and recommend prosecutions. Steinhoff appointed PWC to do a forensic investigation which runs to over 3000 pages. But apart from 11 pages Steinhoff have kept it secret

BRAAM
Now we have a situation where they have spent a couple of million rand to compile a PWC report
Derek
Which is sealed?
Braam
Which Steinhoff is holding close to their chest! Even Jooste has asked them make this thing public so we can see who was all involved and how did this all happen!

Rob Rose
It certainly isn’t acceptable that the full report hasn’t come out. Financial Mail and AmaBhungane have gone to court to compel the full release of that report, because we don’t know what else they haven’t told us



Commentary sixteen
Steinhoff declined an interview. In this written response, the company says its dealing with multiple legal proceedings and it firmly believes its settlement proposal offers claimants a more favourable recovery on their claims, compared to a liquidation.

Ring, ring
Derek
Well it seems Markus Jooste is not going to answer, and according to our media colleagues that is not unusual.

Derek
Should we be bothered as South Africans that three years later no charges have been laid?
Rob
I think we should totally be bothered by that, for one thing it feeds into the conspiracy theory that only black public officials are targeted for wrong doing, and to some extent it’s a reflection on the fact that our forensic capabilities at the NPA aren’t what they could be. We need to prioritize this particular case because the consequence of not doing it properly and timeously would suggest there is no accountability in the private sector and that is not good for local guys, for foreign investment, it’s not good for nobody.

Commentary seventeen
The Steinhoff settlement is steaming ahead in the Netherlands, but Braam and Bernard will have to wait until September to hear whether their application is successful. For Landezwa Dulaze that day cannot come soon enough.

Lendezwa
I believe there is crime that has been committed here. Justice! Justice! Justice! no settlement- justice

THE END.

PROMO ONE
Tekkie Town Founder Braam Van Huysteen sold his business to Steinhoff not for cash but instead for shares. A year later he woke to the biggest corporate scandal in South Africa


PROMO TWO NEW
The Steinhoff crash wiped R200 billion rand off the JSE in a week. Three years later Steinhoff are offering to settle some of the claims. But not everyone is happy.


PROMO THREE
Steinhoff is juggling multiple legal proceedings and R136 billion rand in claims. Now the founder of Tekkie Town has applied to liquidate the former retailing giant.

Bernard They win over, and over, and over again, and that money flows out of the country Commentary Fifteen If they win their court battle they hope the court will order an insolvency inquiry and recommend prosecutions. Steinhoff appointed PWC to do a forensic investigation which runs to over 3000 pages. But apart from 11 pages Steinhoff have kept it secret BRAAM Now we have a situation where they have spent a couple of million rand to compile a PWC report Derek Which is sealed? Braam Which Steinhoff is holding close to their chest! Even Jooste has asked them make this thing public so we can see who was all involved and how did this all happen! Rob Rose It certainly isn’t acceptable that the full report hasn’t come out. Financial Mail and AmaBhungane have gone to court to compel the full release of that report, because we don’t know what else they haven’t told us Commentary sixteen Steinhoff declined an interview. In this written response, the company says its dealing with multiple legal proceedings and it firmly believes its settlement proposal offers claimants a more favourable recovery on their claims, compared to a liquidation. Ring, ring Derek Well it seems Markus Jooste is not going to answer, and according to our media colleagues that is not unusual. Derek Should we be bothered as South Africans that three years later no charges have been laid? Rob I think we should totally be bothered by that, for one thing it feeds into the conspiracy theory that only black public officials are targeted for wrong doing, and to some extent it’s a reflection on the fact that our forensic capabilities at the NPA aren’t what they could be. We need to prioritize this particular case because the consequence of not doing it properly and timeously would suggest there is no accountability in the private sector and that is not good for local guys, for foreign investment, it’s not good for nobody. Commentary seventeen The Steinhoff settlement is steaming ahead in the Netherlands, but Braam and Bernard will have to wait until September to hear whether their application is successful. For Landezwa Dulaze that day cannot come soon enough. Lendezwa I believe there is crime that has been committed here. Justice! Justice! Justice! no settlement- justice THE END. PROMO ONE Tekkie Town Founder Braam Van Huysteen sold his business to Steinhoff not for cash but instead for shares. A year later he woke to the biggest corporate scandal in South Africa PROMO TWO NEW The Steinhoff crash wiped R200 billion rand off the JSE in a week. Three years later Steinhoff are offering to settle some of the claims. But not everyone is happy. PROMO THREE Steinhoff is juggling multiple legal proceedings and R136 billion rand in claims. Now the founder of Tekkie Town has applied to liquidate the former retailing giant. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): In 2016, Braam Van Huysteen sold his company Tekkietown to Steinhoff for R3.2 billion paid for in Steinhoff shares a year later they were almost worthless. Now the race is on to liquidate Steinhoff
metadata.Unique Selling Point: The main players will speak on camera to Carte Blanche. A David and Goliath story in a race against time
metadata.Summary: Imagine this. You spend a lot of time and money and risk building up your unique company. It starts to do well and gets noticed by Markus Jootse, once South Africa’s darling of the business world. The man who you think, has the Midas touch. Markus makes you and your investors an offer for your company in 2016, and instead of paying you cash he offers you shares in one of the richest companies on the JSE and the Frankfurt stock exchange. You agree, you sign the contracts and you get your shares. You have just sold your company for R3.2 Billion Rand, except you opt for shares in Steinhoff instead of the cash. What could possibly go wrong? A year later you get to answer that question when Markus Jooste’s global fraud is exposed, and the once mighty Steinhoff empire comes tumbling down. This is what happened to Braam Van Huyssteen when he sold Tekkie Town to Steinhoff for R3.2 Billion rand. Braam did his due diligence, he went through the books. The accountants said the financial statements fairly reflected the value of the company. Except they didn’t. Markus Jooste may as well have given Braam Van Huyssteen fake bank notes for Tekkie Town. But it was too late – Jooste had already taken Tekkie Town’s shares and funneled them into Steinhoff. Van Huysteen and his investors had basically given away the asset to Jooste for nothing.
metadata.Further information: Now three years later, Jooste is still living a life of luxury, reportedly at Lanzerac near Franschoek, and creditors are scrambling around trying to recoup their money. Complex financial schemes have been put in place in the Netherlands where the bankers look like they will get almost everything back, even though they may have to wait a bit longer than they thought. To make things more opaque Jooste moved Steinhoff International Holdings to the Netherlands. So where does that leave Braam Van Huysteen? Basically nowhere. For a second time the Tekkie Town guys are being fleeced. They want to try and recover what little they can, but they are in a race against time against Dutch law, Steinhoff and some powerful bankers who want it all. Tekkie Town are looking to recover R1.8 billion rand but they will be squeezed out if the matter is heard in a Dutch court next month. THE RACE AGAINST TIME AND THE DUTCH So the Tekkie Town guys are fighting back in a David and Goliath Battle. Last week they launched an urgent application in the Cape High court to have Steinhoff international Holdings liquidated here in South Africa. Former CEO Bernard Mostert signed a comprehensive affidavit that shows just how important this matter still is and the massive effect it can have on many businesses well known to South Africans. We speak to the main players in what is arguably the biggest case of corporate fraud in South African business history.
